title: Debate Arena: Flip the Argument
description: Step into the debate arena where every move is an argument! Place your arguments strategically to flip your opponent's counter-arguments to your side. Master the art of persuasion, logical reasoning, and rhetoric as you dominate the board with compelling discourse.
learning_objectives: Develop persuasion techniques through strategic argument placement
Understand logical reasoning and how to counter opposing viewpoints
Practice rhetoric and the art of changing minds
Learn to identify weak arguments and exploit logical fallacies
Build confidence in constructing compelling arguments
Recognize the importance of positioning in debates
how_to_play: Place your argument disc on the board adjacent to the opponent's counter-argument disc.
Any opponent discs caught in a straight line between your new disc and an existing one are flipped to your side.
You must flip at least one opposing argument with each move — if you can't, your turn is skipped.
Corners are powerful positions that can never be flipped — like an irrefutable argument!
The game ends when neither player can make a valid move.
The player with the most discs on the board wins the debate!

storybook_pages.title: Welcome to the Debate Arena
storybook_pages.text: The grand debate hall is packed. Two sides face off across the argument board, each armed with logic, evidence, and rhetoric. Your goal: convince the audience by flipping opposing viewpoints to your side. Every disc placed is an argument made — every flip, a mind changed.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: grand debate hall with two podiums facing each other, a large game board between them, audience in bleachers, speech bubbles floating in the air, blue and red lighting, dramatic atmosphere, cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: The Art of Persuasion
storybook_pages.text: A strong argument placed in the right position can flip multiple opposing views at once. But beware — your opponent is equally skilled. Corners are like foundational truths that cannot be overturned. Edges provide stable ground. The center is where the fiercest exchanges happen.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: chessboard-like grid with speech bubbles as game pieces, some flipping from red to blue, arrows showing influence spreading across the board, lightbulb moments illustrated, cartoon educational style

storybook_pages.title: Win the Crowd
storybook_pages.text: As the debate nears its end, count your supporters. The side with more arguments on the board wins the hearts and minds of the audience. Remember: it's not just about making arguments — it's about positioning them where they'll have the greatest impact.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: crowd cheering in a debate arena, scoreboard showing argument counts, confetti falling, two debaters shaking hands, speech bubble game pieces covering the board, celebratory cartoon style

transfer_exercises.game_context: Adjusting strategy as the board flips dramatically
transfer_exercises.real_world: Re-evaluating your approach when new information changes the picture

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

achievements.name: Flip Master
achievements.description: Flipped 10+ opponent pieces in a single move

cultural_context: Formal debate culture is strong in Indian educational institutions — from school elocution to Model UN and parliamentary debates at IITs and IIMs. This game builds the strategic argumentation skills that transfer from academic debate to professional persuasion.
reflection_prompt: Which flip changed the shape of the game most? What did you not see coming?
